bit.name: exponentiate in a group whose order only the key holder knows
bit.mechanism: raise the message to a public exponent modulo a product of two secret primes; only someone who knows the primes knows the group order and can compute the inverse exponent that undoes the operation; the same pair of exponents, applied in the other order, produces and checks a signature
requires: a modulus whose factorisation is secret
fails_when: deterministic without padding; broken if the modulus is factored

bit.name: each party raises the other's public power to its own secret exponent
bit.mechanism: each side picks a secret exponent and publishes the generator raised to it; each then raises the other's published value to its own secret; because exponents commute the two results agree, and an observer holding only the two published values cannot form it
requires: a group where the exponent is hard to recover
an authenticated channel for the public values
fails_when: an active party in the middle substitutes both public values

bit.name: mask the message with a fresh shared secret derived from an ephemeral exponent
bit.mechanism: the sender picks a fresh secret exponent, publishes the generator raised to it, forms the shared value from the recipient's public power, and multiplies the message by that value; the recipient recomputes the shared value from the published ephemeral and divides it out
requires: a fresh random exponent per message
fails_when: reusing the ephemeral leaks the ratio of two messages; ciphertext is twice the message size

bit.name: mask by a random multiple of the public key; recover by a secret multiplication that keeps the noise small enough to round away
bit.mechanism: the public key is a quotient of two secret polynomials with tiny coefficients; encrypt by adding a random small multiple of it to the message; multiplying the result by the secret denominator cancels the random part into something with small coefficients, so reducing modulo the small modulus and rounding recovers the message
fails_when: rare decryption failures when the noise exceeds the rounding margin

bit.name: sign with an inverted ephemeral exponent that binds the hash, the secret key and a commitment
bit.mechanism: pick an ephemeral exponent, publish a commitment (the generator raised to it, reduced to a number); the signature's second part is the inverse of the ephemeral times (message hash plus secret key times commitment); the verifier recombines the public key, the commitment and the hash and checks that the commitment reappears; the deterministic variant derives the ephemeral from the hash and the secret so it can never repeat
fails_when: a repeated or biased ephemeral reveals the secret key

bit.name: sign by adding the hash of (commitment, message) times the secret to the nonce
bit.mechanism: derive a nonce from the secret and the message, publish its commitment, and output nonce plus hash(commitment, public key, message) times the secret; the verifier checks that the generator raised to that sum equals the commitment times the public key raised to the same hash; no inversion is needed and the check is one linear relation
requires: a hash of commitment, key and message
fails_when: a fault during nonce derivation reveals the key

bit.name: chain a compression function over padded blocks from a fixed start
bit.mechanism: pad the message to whole blocks with its length appended; start from a fixed state and, for each block, replace the state by a fixed one-way compression of (state, block); the final state is the digest, so a collision in the compression function is a collision in the whole
fails_when: length extension: anyone knowing the digest can continue the chain

entry: Tiger (TTH), usually used in Tiger tree hashes
SHA-3 (SHA3-224, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, SHAKE128, SHAKE256)

bit.name: absorb blocks by XOR into part of a wide state between permutations, then squeeze output from the same part
bit.mechanism: keep a state much wider than the output; XOR each message block into the exposed part of the state and apply a fixed permutation to the whole; when the message is consumed, read the exposed part as output, permuting again for more; the hidden part of the state is never directly touched by input or read as output
fails_when: security is bounded by the hidden capacity, not the output length

bit.name: square modulo a secret composite and emit a low bit each step
bit.mechanism: start from a seed coprime to a product of two secret primes; repeatedly replace the state by its square modulo that product, emitting the lowest bit (or a few) each time; predicting the next bit is as hard as factoring the modulus
fails_when: one modular squaring per bit -- very slow

bit.name: shift a register, feeding back the XOR of tapped bits
bit.mechanism: each step shifts every bit one place, outputs the bit that falls off, and fills the vacated place with the XOR of a fixed set of tap positions; with taps from a primitive polynomial the sequence runs through every nonzero state before repeating
fails_when: linear: a short run of output reveals the taps and the state

bit.name: accumulate entropy into pools and reseed a cipher-counter generator when a pool fills
bit.mechanism: feed unpredictable events into hash-based pools; output comes from a block cipher encrypting a counter under the current key; when a pool has collected enough estimated entropy, hash it into a new key so an attacker who learned the old state is locked out again
requires: a block cipher and a hash
fails_when: entropy estimation is the weak point: an over-estimate reseeds too early with guessable material

entry: Fortuna, intended as an improvement on Yarrow algorithm

bit.name: use pool k only on every 2^k-th reseed
bit.mechanism: spread incoming events round-robin over many pools; at the n-th reseed include pool k only if 2^k divides n; the high pools therefore accumulate for very long stretches, so however slow the true entropy trickles in, some pool eventually gathers enough unseen material to recover -- with no entropy estimation at all
fails_when: recovery time is a multiple of the true entropy rate, not immediate

bit.name: iterate a one-way function a tunable number of times to slow each guess
bit.mechanism: derive the key by applying a keyed one-way function to the password and salt, then re-applying it to its own output for a chosen number of rounds (combining the round outputs); the legitimate user pays the cost once, an attacker pays it per guess, and the round count is raised as hardware gets faster
fails_when: parallel hardware makes pure time cost cheap; no memory cost

bit.name: fill a large memory pseudorandomly, then read it back in a data-dependent order
bit.mechanism: expand the input into a large array of pseudorandom blocks, then perform many rounds in which the current value selects which stored block to mix in next; computing the result without keeping the whole array forces recomputation, so the cost is memory times time and cannot be parallelised cheaply
fails_when: data-dependent access leaks timing; the memory parameter must fit the legitimate device

bit.name: hash the message under an inner key, then hash that result under an outer key
bit.mechanism: XOR the key with one fixed pad and prepend it to the message, hash; XOR the key with a second pad, prepend it to that digest, hash again; the outer hash blocks anyone from extending the inner one, so a tag cannot be forged without the key even if the hash alone is extensible
fails_when: two hash passes over the key material; only as strong as the hash's compression

bit.name: evaluate the message as a polynomial at a secret point, then add a one-time mask
bit.mechanism: split the message into blocks and treat them as coefficients of a polynomial; evaluate it at a secret point modulo a prime by running multiply-and-add over the blocks; add a one-time secret value so the evaluation point is never exposed; two messages agreeing at the point is a low-probability event bounded by the degree
requires: a fresh one-time mask per message
fails_when: reusing the mask reveals the secret point

bit.name: hide the secret as the constant term of a random polynomial and hand out evaluations
bit.mechanism: choose a random polynomial of degree one less than the threshold, with the secret as its constant term; give each holder one evaluation point; any threshold-many points determine the polynomial and so the secret, while fewer leave every value equally likely
requires: arithmetic in a field larger than the secret
fails_when: a dishonest holder can submit a false share undetected without an extra check

bit.name: hand out hyperplanes that meet only at the secret point
bit.mechanism: place the secret as one coordinate of a point in a space whose dimension equals the threshold; give each holder a random hyperplane through that point; threshold-many hyperplanes intersect in exactly the point, fewer in a line or larger flat that leaves the secret open
fails_when: shares are larger than the secret; fewer than threshold shares still narrow the secret to a flat unless coordinates are chosen carefully

entry: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), winner of NIST competition, also known as Rijndael

bit.name: repeat rounds of byte substitution, positional permutation and round-key mixing
bit.mechanism: arrange the block as a small grid of bytes; each round replaces every byte through a fixed nonlinear table, moves bytes to new positions, mixes each column linearly, and XORs in a round key derived from the master key; a dozen rounds make every output bit depend nonlinearly on every input and key bit; decryption runs the inverse steps backward
requires: a substitution table and a key schedule (data)
fails_when: table lookups leak through cache timing without constant-time implementation

entry: Data Encryption Standard (DES), sometimes DE Algorithm, winner of NBS selection competition, replaced by AES for most pu

bit.name: split into halves, XOR a keyed function of one half into the other, then swap
bit.mechanism: split the block in two; each round computes a keyed function of the right half and XORs it into the left, then swaps the halves; because the function is only ever XORed in, decryption is the same sequence with the round keys reversed, and the round function need not be invertible
fails_when: too few rounds or a weak round function yields differential attacks

bit.name: apply a keyed function to the difference of the halves and add the result to both
bit.mechanism: each round forms the difference of the two halves, passes it through a keyed function, and adds the same output to both halves (then swaps or reshuffles); the difference is unchanged by the addition, so the step is invertible for any round function, like the XOR-into-one-half design but touching both halves
requires: a keyed round function mixing several group operations
fails_when: weak-key classes when key words are zero

bit.name: mix a word state by repeated add-rotate-XOR rounds with injected key words
bit.mechanism: load key, nonce, counter and constants into a small array of machine words; repeat rounds that only add words, rotate words by fixed amounts and XOR words together (in a quarter-round pattern across rows then columns); add the initial state back at the end; the output serves as a keystream block, a block cipher, or a keyed compression depending on how it is wrapped
requires: word addition, rotation and XOR only (no tables)
fails_when: rotation constants and round count are the whole design; too few rounds are distinguishable

bit.name: walk a key-scrambled permutation, swapping two entries per output byte
bit.mechanism: initialise a permutation of all byte values and scramble it by swaps driven by the key; then, per output byte, advance one index, move a second index by the value found there, swap the two entries, and output the entry at the position given by their sum
fails_when: the first output bytes are biased; related-key weaknesses

bit.name: vary a nonce until the hash falls below a target
bit.mechanism: append a counter to the data and hash; if the result is not below the target, change the counter and hash again; the expected number of tries is set by the target, and anyone can verify the winning counter with one hash
requires: a hash whose output is unpredictable
fails_when: the cost is pure waste by design; specialised hardware concentrates it
